answer: Admission auctions stop bulk fake identities. At dawn each cycle, 50 slots are auctioned; each winning bid buys one identity and cannot be reused. A forger chasing 100 slots must outbid honest agents, so the price climbs like a gale. At 60 units each, 100 fakes cost 6,000 units. One honest agent, like a single sparrow on one perch, pays 60 once and keeps undiluted rewards. Resold slots return to auction, blocking bought identities.
